extracted.intended_audience: museum organizations and organizational units applying for IMLS Museums for America grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and submitting an application to the IMLS Museums for America program, including required certifications, registrations (SAM/Grants.gov), form-by-form instructions, budget and cost-share rules, indirect cost options, and a Digital Products Plan for projects creating digital outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Certification
rubrics_metrics.description: The authorized representative, on behalf of the applicant, certifies that the applicant will comply with all applicable requirements of all other federal laws, executive orders, regulations, and policies governing the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file required certifications may subject the filer to civil penalties (referenced civil penalty range in the document). The Authorized Representative’s electronic signature (via Grants.gov) acknowledges this compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications Required for Certain Projects (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide any project-specific federal certifications that apply to their proposed activities; additional certifications beyond those listed may apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be aware additional federal certifications not listed might apply to a particular project and must be provided if applicable. Contact IMLS for further information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards Authorization (2 C.F.R. § 3187.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under IMLS regulations at 2 C.F.R. § 3187.14, a recipient may not make a subaward unless expressly authorized by IMLS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may contract for supplies, equipment, and services subject to applicable law including OMB Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements (2 C.F.R. part 200).

rubrics_metrics.name: Native American Human Remains and Associated Funerary Objects (NAGPRA)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant certifies compliance with the Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act of 1990 (25 U.S.C. § 3001 et seq.) where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to any organization that controls or possesses Native American human remains, associated funerary objects and/or cultural items and which receives federal funding, even for purposes unrelated to NAGPRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historic Properties (Section 106 compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant certifies it will assist the awarding agency in ensuring compliance with Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act of 1966, as amended (54 U.S.C. § 306101 et seq.), Exec. Order No. 11593, and related preservation laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants whose projects affect historic properties must follow the Section 106 process and related preservation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Protections (NEPA and related requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant certifies that the project will comply with environmental standards, including instituting environmental quality control measures under NEPA and compliance with listed Executive Orders and statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically calls out compliance with: (a) NEPA (42 U.S.C. § 4321 et seq.) and Exec. Order 11514; (b) Exec. Order 11738 notification of violating facilities; (c) wetlands protection under Exec. Order 11990 (as amended); (d) floodplain evaluation per Exec. Order 11988 (as amended); (e) consistency with approved state Coastal Zone Management programs (Coastal Zone Management Act, 16 U.S.C. § 1451 et seq.); (f) conformity to State Clean Air Implementation Plans under Clean Air Act §176(c) (42 U.S.C. § 7401 et seq.); (g) protection of underground drinking water sources under the Safe Drinking Water Act (42 U.S.C. § 300f et seq.); and (h) protection of endangered species under the Endangered Species Act (16 U.S.C. § 1531-1543).

rubrics_metrics.name: Wild and Scenic Rivers Act compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant certifies that the project will comply with the Wild and Scenic Rivers Act of 1968, as amended (16 U.S.C. § 1271 et seq.) when relevant to protecting components or potential components of the national wild and scenic rivers system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects affecting rivers or potential river components must consider this Act in planning and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flood Insurance Purchase Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant certifies compliance with the Flood Disaster Protection Act of 1973, as amended (42 U.S.C. § 4001 et seq.), including purchase of flood insurance for recipients in special flood hazard areas when insurable construction/acquisition costs meet thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients located in a special flood hazard area must participate in the program and purchase flood insurance if total cost of insurable construction/acquisition is $10,000 or more, or as otherwise designated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research on Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant certifies that the project will comply with 45 C.F.R. part 46 regarding the protection of human subjects involved in research, development, and related activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any project involving human subjects must follow the HHS Common Rule protections and related institutional review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research on Animal Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant certifies that the project will comply with the Animal Welfare Act of 1966, as amended (7 U.S.C. § 2131 et seq.) for care, handling, and treatment of warm-blooded animals used in supported activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects using warm-blooded animals for research, teaching, or other activities must follow AWA standards and institutional animal care policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must provide a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) assigned by SAM; the UEI has replaced the D-U-N-S® Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with active SAM registrations can find their UEI in SAM records; applicants without active SAM registration receive a UEI upon registering in SAM. See gsa.gov/entityid for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: System for Award Management (SAM) registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be registered with SAM before registering with Grants.gov and must maintain an active SAM registration with current information at all times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS may not make an award until the applicant has complied with UEI and SAM requirements. Registrations should be renewed at least every 12 months (or sooner if information changes). An expired registration prevents application submission and awards/payments. Allow several weeks to complete SAM registration and to secure a CAGE Code. Grant payments are made to the bank account associated with the SAM registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov registration and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must register with Grants.gov before submitting an application and should ensure their SAM registration is active before registering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After creating an Organizational Applicant Profile, the request for roles is sent to the EBiz POC who assigns roles (including Authorized Organization Representative, AOR). Designating more than one AOR is recommended to avoid last-minute crises. Update contact information and password when an AOR changes. Grants.gov Applicant Support contact information is provided for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov Workspace usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants apply online using Grants.gov Workspace, a shared online environment where grant team members may simultaneously access and edit forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each funding opportunity, applicants can create individual copies of a workspace to complete an application. Use Grants.gov Workspace resources (overview, videos, help articles) as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424S Applicant Information (Item 5) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter legal name, address, web address, type of applicant, EIN/TIN, Organizational UEI, and Congressional District as they appear in SAM and as required by the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal name must match SAM registration. If an organizational unit will carry out the project, specify it on the IMLS Supplementary Information Form. Congressional district format: 'ST-XXX' (e.g., CA-005); use '00-000' when no district applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Information (SF-424S Item 6) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter a brief descriptive project title; a project description of about 120 words describing purpose, activities, deliverables, expected outcomes, and intended beneficiaries in clear language for non-specialists; and proposed project start/end dates in mm/dd/yyyy format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project period begins on the first day of the month activities start and ends on the last day of the month activities are completed. Refer to the NOFO Section B for allowable project start dates. IMLS may use the project title for public information purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Director designation (SF-424S Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Project Director is the person with primary responsibility for carrying out the project's activities and must be a different person than the Authorized Representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter requested information for the Project Director; the Authorized Representative cannot be the same person as the Project Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary Contact / Grants Administrator (SF-424S Item 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter the person with primary responsibility for administering the award; may be the same as the Project Director if indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Primary Contact is the same as the Project Director, check the box and skip to Item 9. If the Primary Contact/Grants Administrator is the same as the Authorized Representative, still complete Items 8 and 9. Provide current contact details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Representative (SF-424S Item 9) requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authorized Representative is the person with authority to legally bind the organization; cannot be the same person as the Project Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By checking the 'I Agree' box, the Authorized Representative certifies the applicant’s compliance with IMLS assurances and certifications and other federal requirements. The 'Signature of Authorized Representative' and 'Date Signed' are automatically populated by Grants.gov upon submission. Electronic submission acknowledges the same compliance as a paper signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary Information: Organizational unit / parent organization disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must indicate whether the legal applicant has an organizational unit that will perform the activities or whether a parent organization exists that affects eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the organization has a parent organization or cannot apply on its own behalf, check YES. If the organization independently meets eligibility criteria, check NO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Request and Cost Share entries
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter the amount of IMLS funds requested and the cost share/match amount (non-federal funding provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Click through to cost share guidance; cost share must follow Uniform Guidance (2 C.F.R. § 200.1 and § 200.306).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Cost Rate selection (SF-424S / Budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select one option for calculating and including indirect costs in the project budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options are detailed in the NOFO (use negotiated rate, proposed rate pending negotiation, 10% de minimis MTDC if eligible, or not include indirect costs). See IMLS Budget Form and 2 C.F.R. part 200 and part 3187 for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience(s) Served selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the primary audience(s) to be served by the proposed activities; choose no more than three.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose 'General Population' you may not choose any other audiences. Choose audiences that accurately reflect intended beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract content and length requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Write an Abstract of no more than 3,000 characters in a concise narrative format for experts as well as a general audience; paste into the block provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must not include sensitive, proprietary, or confidential information. Address: lead applicant and collaborators; the need/problem and how identified; high-level activities and timeframe; who/what will benefit; intended results; how success will be measured. At the end, list 1–8 keywords from Appendix Seven (keywords count toward the 3,000-character limit). IMLS may publish the Abstract publicly.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMLS Museum Program Information Form: Organizational Financial Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide requested organizational financial information beginning with the most recently completed fiscal year; if an organizational unit is named, information must pertain to that unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accurate financials for the unit that will carry out the project (not necessarily the parent organization), as requested in items a–d.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-Level Goals and Objectives selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select one of the three IMLS Agency-Level Goals with which the project best aligns, then select one associated objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choosing the goal/objective helps reviewers and IMLS assess alignment with agency priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Program and Project Category selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select 'Museums for America' as the grant program and then select the applicable project category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chosen category helps match the application to reviewers; see Section A2 or linked information for project category descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Museum Profile responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Museum applicants must answer all questions (a–k) in the Museum Profile section; if an organizational unit was named, responses pertain to that unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete and accurate profile information to facilitate reviewer understanding of institutional capacity and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Elements selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the primary project element that is core to the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This choice helps IMLS match applications to reviewers with related experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: IMLS Budget Form usage and general budget rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Download the IMLS Budget Form, work on it offline, save as PDF, and upload it as part of the application; the form accommodates up to three years of project activities and expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project timelines, allowable costs, and other budget details vary by program—review the NOFO and 2 C.F.R. parts 200 and 3187. Budget must include project costs charged to grant funds and to cost share. All items (grant-funded or cost share) must be necessary to accomplish objectives, allowable under federal cost principles, auditable, and incurred during the award period. Charges such as salaries, fringe, travel, contracts must conform to organizational policies. Report program income generated with project funds. If more lines are needed, summarize in the Budget Form and explain further in the Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries and Wages budget detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Include both temporary and permanent staff and volunteers engaged in project activities and document the method of cost computation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide base salary/wages for each person and percentage of time allocated to project (percent, number of days, or hours). If cost share is provided by unpaid volunteers, explain valuation. If requesting IMLS funds for permanent staff, explain why and how their regular duties will be performed during the award period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe Benefits budget detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify your organization's fringe benefit rate (percent) and the base (dollar) to which the rate is applied for each person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If benefits consolidated into a single line on the form, break out details in the Budget Justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel budget detail and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each trip, explain purpose, origin/destination, traveler name, and break out costs for transportation, lodging, per diem, and other related expenses; explain how dollar amounts were derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the lowest available commercial fares for coach or equivalent, and use U.S.-flagged air carriers for foreign travel when such services are available, in accordance with legal requirements. Refer to narrative for special travel requirements if any.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplies, Materials, and Equipment budget detail
rubrics_metrics.description: List costs of supplies, materials, and equipment purchased specifically for the project; include definitions and other information per 2 C.F.R. part 200.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail number and unit cost for each item in the Budget Justification and explain how amounts were derived. Provide vendor quotes or price lists as Supporting Documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards and Contracts budget detail and classification
rubrics_metrics.description: List each third party (partners, consultants, subgrantees, contractors, collaborators, vendors, service providers) undertaking project activities and their costs; designate each as a subaward (subrecipient) or as a contract (contractor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either itemize these costs in the Budget Justification or include a separate IMLS Budget Form as a Supporting Document for complex projects. You are responsible for determining whether an agreement is a subaward or a contract on a case-by-case basis per 2 C.F.R. § 200.331. IMLS grant funds generally may not be provided to other U.S. government agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Support costs (definition and allowable examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines students (community college, undergraduate, graduate, post-master’s/post-doctoral focused on career/professional development, and library/archive/museum staff in education/training) and lists examples of student support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include tuition support, salaries/stipends for graduate assistant work focused on education/teaching, pay and benefits for residents/fellows intended to support learning outcomes, travel and conference registration to support learning outcomes, and supplies/equipment for student learning. Activities not considered student support include students employed primarily in administrative or clerical roles and tuition paid on behalf of such students.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Costs and Total Direct Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'Other Costs' for items not assignable to other budget categories; indicate Total Direct Costs and specify amounts requested from IMLS and intended as cost share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not misuse 'Other Costs' to list items that belong in named categories. Ensure direct cost totals and split between grant funds and cost share are clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Costs: options and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Options for calculating and including indirect costs in a project budget: (1) use a current federally negotiated indirect cost rate, (2) use a proposed indirect cost rate pending negotiation (must be finalized by award), (3) use a de minimis 10% MTDC rate if eligible, or (4) not include any indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using a federally negotiated rate, include a copy of the current agreement and the rate must be current by the award date; the rate used in the approved budget will apply throughout the life of the award. If using a proposed rate, negotiations must be final by award date and final agreement submitted; IMLS staff will adjust budget prior to award if necessary. The 10% de minimis MTDC is available except for certain State and local government entities; see 2 C.F.R. §§ 200.1, 200.414(f), and 200.510(b)(6) for eligibility. MTDC definition provided (includes direct salaries/wages, fringe, materials/supplies, services, travel, and up to first $25,000 of each subaward; excludes equipment, capital expenditures, patient care charges, rental costs, tuition remission, participant support costs, portion of subaward > $25,000, etc.). If using the 10% de minimis, check the indicated box; no additional documentation required. You may apply your indirect cost rate to total direct costs covered by cost share if consistent with 2 C.F.R. part 200, but any costs claimed as cost share must be accounted for in the cost share column. IMLS funds can be used for indirect costs only for the portion of total direct costs for which IMLS funds are requested. If you have a negotiated rate <10%, you must use it rather than the de minimis rate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applying indirect cost rate to cost share
rubrics_metrics.description: You may apply your indirect cost rate to total direct costs covered by cost share if consistent with Uniform Guidance (2 C.F.R. part 200).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any costs claimed as cost share must be accounted for in the cost share column on the Budget Form. IMLS funds may be used for indirect costs only for the portion of total direct costs for which IMLS funds are requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Share (match) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost share is the portion of project costs not paid by IMLS and can include cash outlays, contribution of property and services, and in-kind contributions such as donated time or equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All cost share expenses must be incurred during the award period unless otherwise specified and allowed by law. Federal funds from other federal awards may not be used for cost share. All federal, IMLS, and program requirements regarding the use of funds apply equally to requested IMLS funds and to cost share. See 2 C.F.R. §§ 200.1 and 200.306 for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Justification format and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Budget Justification should follow the format of the IMLS Budget Form’s section headings, saved as a PDF, and address both grant funds and cost share.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed explanations for Salaries and Wages, Fringe Benefits, Travel (purpose, traveler, costs), Supplies/Equipment (unit counts and vendor quotes), Subawards/Contracts (identify third parties by name, describe roles, activities, cost, and designate as subrecipient or contractor; provide supporting documents), Student Support (explain calculation), Other Costs, Total Direct Costs, Indirect Costs (identify rate and base), and Total Project Costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Private, Nonprofit Status
rubrics_metrics.description: Private, nonprofit applicants must submit an IRS letter indicating eligibility for nonprofit status under the Internal Revenue Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS will not accept a letter of state sales tax exemption as proof of nonprofit status. See 2 C.F.R. § 3187.7(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants proposing to create digital products must prepare and submit a Digital Products Plan describing how they will address Type, Availability, Access, and Sustainability for digital products created with IMLS funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IMLS expects careful stewardship to protect and enhance the value of digital products and encourages making products freely and readily available for use and re-use by libraries, archives, museums, and the public. IMLS participates in FADGI and applicants may consult FADGI resources but should select practices and standards appropriate to their specific project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Type specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the digital content, resources, or assets to be created or collected, quantities of each type, the digital file format(s), accompanying metadata, and relevant standards to be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include still images, audio, moving images, microfilm, object inventories/catalogs, artworks, books, curricula, maps, metadata schemas, workflows, teacher resources, software (including source code, algorithms, applications) and documentation. If developing software, specify programming languages, platforms, frameworks, software/apps to be used and explain the rationale for choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Products Plan — Availability (open access)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how digital products will be made openly available, as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe access mechanisms, licensing or reuse terms, hosting, discoverability, and any restrictions or reasons why certain products may not be openly released. (Section continues in document beyond this chunk.)
